analysis:
Examined the docs/developer/test.md changes (head lines 844, 854-860, 926) and the one-line code change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/ModelBenchmarkNativeQwen4.swift (head lines 38-40).

The docs changes add FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests and ModelBenchmarkDispatchTests to the focused selector list. They also add a paragraph describing a test that builds a tiny Flint through the production slot factory with default settings, and state that Flint is paged-only so DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND may only be unset or 'paged'. The prose says persistent caching is disabled only for fixture isolation. This is test documentation with no runtime effect and does not weaken any control. It never suggests production cache roots or keys, and it keeps the existing isolation warnings.

The code change adds modelType == "flint" to a model-type predicate in ModelBenchmarkNativeQwen4.swift. The predicate already includes qwen4-exp, prism_hadamard_qwen35 and mimo_v2, and the comment says scalar generate would run Flint's non-paged scalar caches. Only the predicate body is visible. The enclosing function name and its callers are not in the supplied evidence, so I can't confirm the exact routing. It most plausibly routes Flint benchmarks to the native paged path rather than scalar generate. It sits in the ProviderBenchmark tooling and touches no coordinator wire contract, key handling, attestation or authorization. The benchmark path is operator-run and local.

Relevant threat T-041 (prefix cache). The benchmark routing change does not alter the SSD cache TTL, HMAC lookup, salt scoping or purge. The doc describes disabling persistent caching in the fixture, which is test-only.

Remaining unverified: the predicate's callers and the benchmark dispatch semantics. These are tooling-level and do not affect a security conclusion I could establish. No findings.
